speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Snow on the sill, and the pot is hot. Sit while you are still a man who has not gone out. Two of the clock was yesterday's hour, and I suppose today is the same kind of day.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Today is the other play. Two of the clock. The snow can thin a yard. It does not change the hour.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Shall I put your boots to the fire, sir? The lane is white at the edges. I have not been out in it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Put them to the fire. I am not going yet. The letter on the desk stays there. Thursday's carrier, not this morning's errand.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I was not going to give it to a stranger in the snow. Mark me. A letter that has waited since Sunday can wait until the man whose trade it is. Eat. Board is threepence, snow or no snow.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Threepence, then. And I am not talking of yesterday at this table. The play is the play. The rest of the week can keep until I am back.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I shall not ask about the cook again. Mistress says I had my answer, and the answer was down the stair. I only want to know if the snow gets into the yard where you stand.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Alse. Bread. He will stand where the company stands, and he will come home wet or he will not. We are not a window on Gracechurch Street.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The yard will be thinner if the snow holds. I have played to thinner. Thank you for the fire. I will be gone after noon, and back when the reckoning is done.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then the reckoning is theirs, and the boots are yours. Do not bring me a purse to count on the kitchen board. I count candles and loaves. I do not count players' shares.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The loaf was a finger short again. I set it to the notch before you came down. A penny, mistress said, and not a word more about it on a snow morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A penny is enough to say. You have both been kind. I am going up to the letter, to see that it is still the letter, and then I am done with paper until tonight.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: See that it is the same sheet. I will not have you add a page because the lane is white and you are restless.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not add a page. The question is answered. The day is not named. It goes on the twenty-seventh, and not with a man I hail in the snow.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Is the afternoon the king again, sir, the one with the crooked back? You were out in him on Tuesday.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The same king. I am in it. The snow may keep some of them at home. That is the weather's affair, and Heminges will count what comes.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Let him count it at the inn. I have said so. A purse on this board would put me in a trade I did not let the room for.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No purse. I will bring myself back, wet or not, when the reckoning is done. Edith's paper is their paper. It is not a bill of this house.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I do not know a Mistress Edith, sir.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: And you need not. Bread, Alse. He has a play at two and a letter that is finished. Two facts are enough for a snow morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two facts, and the threepence. I am done. The boots can come off the fender when I am ready, and not before.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: They will be warm, sir.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Warm boots and a cold yard. That is a player's bargain, and he knew it when he sat down. Eat the crust. It is the short end, and it is paid for.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am eating it. A penny, a finger short, and threepence for the sitting. I can say grace over that and be done.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then be done, and go up to your letter. The snow will wait. It has nowhere else to be.
